title: Delight in the details
principle: Spend care on micro-interactions, focus states, and edge copy that most users only notice when missing—polish is a signal of respect.
procedure: List five moments a careful user will touch (focus, empty, error, success, hover).
Design each moment intentionally; ban default browser leftovers where brand matters.
Add one surprise of restraint (not fireworks)—timing, easing, or copy.
Verify keyboard and reduced-motion paths feel equally considered.
Cut any delight that slows a frequent action (novelty vs frequency).
examplePrompts:
Polish the five touch moments on this UI: focus, empty, error, success, hover.

For each: intended feel in 5 words; motion ≤200ms or none; copy rewrite.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do not add confetti to primary flows.
promptWhy: Turns vague ‘make it nice’ into a checklist of moments.
tips: Comeau’s public writing obsesses over CSS details that feel good in the hand.
Pair with Rauno’s novelty restraint for high-frequency actions.

workedExamples.title: Default focus ring shame
workedExamples.after: Visible, on-brand focus that still passes contrast.

workedExamples.title: Empty state shrug
workedExamples.after: One human sentence + one clear next action.
workedExamples.body: Empty states are product moments, not absences.

antiPatterns: Delight on the most frequent action that needs speed.
checklist: No noisy delight on high-frequency actions.
